The standard Payne derivation $W(3,7)^P$ has **343 derived points** ($PG(3,7) \setminus P^\perp$, where $|PG(3,7)| = 400$ and $|P^\perp| = 57$). A partial ovoid in this geometry has size **at most 42**, because adjoining $P$ yields a partial ovoid in $W(3,7)$ of size $\le 43$ (Tallini bound). (2026) for the opposite product construction is C. Delorme, *Large bipartite graphs with given degree and diameter*, J. Graph Theory **9**(3) (1985), 325–334 (DOI: 10.1002/jgt.3190090304). Full text was unobtainable via available electronic channels; thus, whether JGT 1985 already includes this spread-fill augmentation or whether it is an immediate corollary cannot be confirmed or ruled out. - **Verdict on Novelty/Priority:** Strictly **UNKNOWN**. If the filled $160050$ source is already present in JGT 1985, the +50 margin against published literature becomes 0. - Mathematical and formal correctness of the 15 graphs is fully established (**PASS**), but global priority or world-record status is **NOT certified**. 3. **Draft Package Status:** - The expert draft document [P33_FIFTEEN_RESULTS_20261101_DRAFT_RECEIPT.json](file:///inspire/hdd/global_user/mahaitong-240108120090/ar4math/expert_review_current/P33_FIFTEEN_RESULTS_20261101_DRAFT_RECEIPT.json#L1-L44) remains in `DRAFT_FIFTEEN_RESULTS_READABLE_NOT_FROZEN` status. - Completion of this Checkpoint C mathematical review **must not** trigger automated freezing of the expert draft or packaging of the ZIP artifact.
